title: Two-stage Miller OTA
description: The classic two-stage Miller operational transconductance amplifier: a differential input stage (input pair + current-mirror load) driving a common-source second stage, with a compensation capacitor $C_c$ bridging the second stage (Miller pole-splitting). $C_c$ is the compensation knob: it sets the dominant pole and hence the unity-gain bandwidth GBW = $g_{m1}/(2*\pi*C_c)$. The feedforward path through $C_c$ creates a right-half-plane zero $z = g_{m2}/C_c$ that erodes phase; the $R_z = 1/g_{m2}$ nulling resistor removes it. The phase-margin and second-pole rows are ESTIMATE-grade small-signal approximations for sizing intuition — the simulator owns stability sign-off. Children evaluate in dependency order: the stage-1 mirror load first (diode-bound — at DC balance the mirror's output side sits at exactly the diode drop, which is also the zero-systematic-offset condition, so the stage-1 output DC is $VDD - |V_{GS,ld1}|$ by construction rather than a number to retune), then the input device, then the stage-2 device and its load. Entered from the COMMON MODE like the 5T: the input pair's tail node is pinned so the produced $CM_{in}$ equals $CM_{dc}$, fixing the pair's body bias and drain-source voltage outright. On the demo NMOS table every device sizes against the same data, so the stage-2 sign param stays at +1.

params.name: PM_target
params.note: phase-margin target; the PM row is estimate-grade

params.name: C1_est
params.note: stage-1 output node cap (stage-2 gate + drain parasitics + wiring); refine from the stage-2 device cgg plus extraction

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: the input common mode the application presents. The engine places the tail node so the sheet sits exactly here; sweep it to trace the common-mode axis This sheet carries NO containment edges: stage 1 does not close on sky130-class supplies at these defaults, and a range claim that cannot be tuned honestly would be theater — see the single-stage OTAs for the pattern.

params.name: V_tail
params.note: the input pair's tail node. Solved rather than set: bisected between min and max (the BRACKET) until the produced common mode equals CM_dc. Fixes the pair's body bias and drain-source voltage in one stroke. Both bracket ends must leave the pair drain-source voltage under the mirror diode drop — on a process whose PMOS diode eats most of the rail, the pin will say so, and raising gm_id_ld1 (a smaller diode drop) is the knob that reopens it

params.name: Cc
params.note: Miller compensation cap: sets the dominant pole and GBW = gm1/(2*pi*Cc)

params.name: V_out2
params.note: stage-2 output DC level; sets both stage-2 devices' vds

params.name: out_sign
params.note: vds sign of the stage-2 device table (PMOS common source): +1 for the N-style demo axis, -1 for a signed-PMOS axis

doc.title: Stage-1 mirror-load device
doc.description: One side of the stage-1 current-mirror load at half the tail current, DIODE-bound: at DC balance the mirror's output side sits at the same drain voltage as its diode side (the zero-systematic-offset condition), so the vds = vgs diagonal is the honest operating point for both. Its drop sets the stage-1 output DC; its output conductance loads the first-stage gain.

doc.title: Stage-1 input-pair device
doc.description: Half-circuit input device at half the tail current. Its source sits at the tail node — that is its body bias — and its drain one mirror diode drop below VDD, so its drain-source voltage is what is left between the two.

doc.title: Stage-2 common-source device
doc.description: The second-stage gain device carrying the full stage-2 current at the output DC level. Its gm sets the RHP zero, the second pole, and the nulling resistor; its gate capacitance dominates the stage-1 output node cap.

params.name: vx
params.note: signed to this table's axis convention

rows.name: CM_in
rows.note: the input common mode this bias produces — an OUTPUT here, not a setting; rises monotonically with the tail node, so the pin is a well-posed bisection

rows.name: V1
rows.note: stage-1 output DC — the mirror diode drop below the supply, by construction rather than retuned: at balance the mirror's output side sits exactly there (also the zero-systematic-offset condition)

rows.name: gm2
rows.note: stage-2 transconductance: sets the RHP zero, the second pole, and the nulling resistor

rows.name: GBW
rows.note: Miller-compensated unity-gain bandwidth (input gm into the compensation cap)

rows.name: wc
rows.note: angular unity-gain crossover (2*pi*GBW), the frequency the phase-margin estimate is read at

rows.name: z_rhp
rows.note: the right-half-plane zero the feedforward path through Cc would place, kept as a reference point for the UNCOMPENSATED stage: the Rz = 1/gm2 nulling resistor below moves it to infinity, which is why the phase-margin row carries no zero term

rows.name: p2
rows.note: non-dominant (output) pole ESTIMATE; C1_est is the stage-1 output-node cap — refine it from the stage-2 cgg plus extraction

rows.name: Rz
rows.note: nulling resistor Rz = 1/gm2 that moves the RHP zero to infinity

rows.name: PM
rows.note: ESTIMATE: crossover phase lag from the second pole alone, because the Rz = 1/gm2 nulling resistor removes the RHP zero. The simulator owns stability sign-off

rows.name: SR
rows.note: the smaller slew limit: stage-1 tail charging Cc, or stage-2 current charging CL

rows.name: Av1
rows.note: stage-1 gain into the input-device and mirror-load output conductances

rows.name: Rout
rows.note: the resistance the amplifier presents at its output — stage two's own output conductance in parallel with its load device's. The gain assumes a capacitive load, so nothing here models a resistive one; this row is what a composing parent checks its own loading against

rows.name: Av2
rows.note: stage-2 common-source gain into its own and the load conductances

rows.name: Av
rows.note: two-stage DC gain (product of the stage gains)

rows.name: cgg2
rows.note: stage-2 gate capacitance — the dominant term in the stage-1 output cap C1_est; compare to refine the estimate

rows.name: cgg_in
rows.note: estimate: the capacitance one input terminal presents — the gate capacitance of a single input device. Gate capacitance only, because the Miller term needs the gate-drain fraction and these tables do not carry it, so a driving stage sees more than this. No rule reads it

rows.name: I_q
rows.note: estimate: quiescent supply current — the first-stage tail plus the output branch. The datasheet line for comparing designs; no rule reads it

rules.note: two-stage DC gain meets the target
the worse of the two slew limits meets the target
the compensated bandwidth (gm1/(2*pi*Cc)) meets the target
ESTIMATE-grade phase margin; the simulator owns the real stability sign-off

where the RHP zero would sit WITHOUT the nulling resistor: above crossover (equivalently gm2 >= gm1), or an uncompensated version of this stage loses its phase margin. With Rz = 1/gm2 in place the zero is gone and this is a design-margin reading, not a stability condition
stage-2 device saturated at the output DC level
stage-2 load saturated at the output DC level
trips when the tail node is pushed so high the pair runs out of drain-source voltage under the mirror diode drop — lower gm/ID on the mirror spends less of it

the stage-2 gate sits at V1 = VDD - |vgs_ld1|, so stage 2 carries its intended current only when its own |vgs| at (I2, gm_id_s2) matches the mirror diode drop — the classic W/L-ratio condition. Retune gm_id_s2 or I2 until these agree, or the second stage sits at a different current than the sheet assumes
